clue.text: Knightly combat judge originally saw during excursion

indicators.note: during says the letter sits within the word for the trip, splitting it

parts.note: an outing is a short excursion or trip

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word saw, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of saw

explanation.surface: A judge first saw knights tilting while away on a day trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Jousting was the mounted lance contest fought between medieval knights in tournaments.

clue.text: Young kangaroo's energy observed in delight

indicators.note: observed in says the physics symbol is seen inside the word for delight

parts.note: joy is great delight

explanation.surface: A baby kangaroo is energetic and a delight to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Joey is the Australian name for a young marsupial, especially a baby kangaroo still in the pouch.

clue.text: Army group using a Continental method of getting info

parts.note: un is the French for a, French being a language of the Continent
IT, information technology, is a modern way of obtaining information

explanation.surface: A military intelligence unit gathers information the European way.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a formation or detachment of soldiers within an army.

clue.text: Our one quest, oddly, finding semiprecious stone

indicators.note: oddly says the letters are arranged in a strange way, so they are mixed up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An adventurer's peculiar search ends with a semiprecious gem being found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' tempts you to take the odd letters of the phrase, but they do not work; here it signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Turquoise is an opaque blue-green mineral prized as a gemstone of lesser value than precious stones.

clue.text: Unnecessary, one's former nurse dipping into faulty Latin

indicators.note: dipping into says the following words go inside the mixed-up letters
faulty says the word Latin is broken and its letters must be rearranged

parts.note: SEN was a State Enrolled Nurse, a UK qualification now discontinued

explanation.surface: A retired nurse's poor Latin is deemed superfluous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nonessential is not required, so it is unnecessary; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Trinket initially greeted eagerly, with gratitude as well

indicators.note: initially says each word that follows contributes only its first letter

parts.words: greeted eagerly, with gratitude as well
parts.note: the first letters of these six words, read in order

explanation.surface: A cheap gift is welcomed with enthusiasm and thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A gewgaw is a showy but worthless ornament or bauble, much like a trinket.

clue.text: Resinous substance contributing to travel emissions

indicators.note: contributing to says the letters form part of the words travel emissions

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of travel and the start of emissions

explanation.surface: Some gooey stuff adds to the pollution caused by transport.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant gum resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and ointments.

clue.text: Pulverised head of angleworm in part: it should attract fish

parts.note: pulverised means ground into powder

indicators.note: in says that letter sits inside the word for part

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece

indicators.note: head of picks the leading letter of angleworm

parts.note: the first letter of angleworm

explanation.surface: A crushed-up worm makes an effective lure for anglers.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundbait is bait scattered into the water to draw fish to the angler's swim.

clue.text: Shrink back, but ultimately accept blue cotton fabric

parts.note: to wince is to flinch or shrink back
yet can mean but, as in 'small yet strong'

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the two following words

parts.note: the last letters of accept and blue

explanation.surface: Someone recoils but finally takes a blue cotton cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Winceyette is a soft brushed cotton cloth used especially for nightwear and sheets.

clue.text: Expat given award by old record company

parts.note: EMI was a major British record label
a grant is a sum awarded

explanation.surface: An expatriate wins a prize from a former record label.
explanation.walkthrough: EMI was a famous British record company, home of the Beatles.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant has left their home country to live abroad, as an expat has.

clue.text: Acclaim part of speech picked up by military engineers

parts.note: RE are the Royal Engineers of the British Army

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: a noun is one of the parts of speech

explanation.surface: Army engineers overhear a fragment of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is fame or wide acclaim, the honour of being celebrated.

clue.text: Stirrer primarily targeting earner in Vladivostok, say?

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of targeting

parts.note: the first letter of targeting
in a Russian city money is roubles, so an earner there is a rouble maker

explanation.surface: An agitator goes after a Russian wage-earner.
explanation.walkthrough: Vladivostok is a Russian city, where the currency is the rouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrer is someone who deliberately causes trouble or dissent, a troublemaker.

clue.text: Lowliness of press employee given directions in Mass, say

parts.note: a sub, or sub-editor, works on a newspaper

indicators.note: in places the directions inside the word for the church rite

parts.note: Mass is an example of a church service
E and N are two compass directions

explanation.surface: A journalist is told where to go during Mass and feels humble.
explanation.definitionFit: Subservience is servile submissiveness, the state of being humble or lowly before others.

clue.text: Resolved to eat with daughter around end of college session

indicators.note: around says the eating word and daughter wrap round what follows

parts.note: to dine is to eat a meal

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of college

parts.note: the last letter of college
a term is an academic session

explanation.surface: Someone decided to have dinner with their daughter as the college term ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Determined means firmly resolved, having made up one's mind.

clue.text: Bounder supporting Bury, an uninvited guest

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits below, so it comes after

parts.note: to inter is to bury
a loper is one who runs with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: A cad from Bury turns up at a party unasked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' and 'Bury' suggest a cad and the Lancashire town, but they are a runner and the verb to bury.
explanation.definitionFit: An interloper is someone who intrudes where they are not wanted.

clue.text: Boredom shown by Greek character in key part of UK

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: in places the Greek letter inside the abbreviation

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, part of the UK
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A bored Greek is spotted in a corner of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness and dissatisfaction, a word borrowed from French for boredom.

clue.text: Even-handed sailor left in East? Absolutely

indicators.note: in puts the sailor and left inside the word for absolutely

parts.note: quite can mean absolutely, as in 'quite right'
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A fair-minded sailor stays out East, absolutely.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitable means fair and impartial, treating all sides justly.

clue.text: Attempt's sound by early settlers making percussion instruments?

indicators.note: sound says we want letters that are heard like the word for attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
the Angles were Germanic settlers in early England

explanation.surface: Pioneers try making drums and other noisy instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angles settled in Britain after the Romans left and gave England its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a steel rod bent into shape and struck in an orchestra; the question mark flags the plural form.

clue.text: Basic Lent meal prepared by English

indicators.note: prepared, as a cook prepares food, says the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An Englishman cooks a simple meal for Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means fundamental or rudimentary, relating to first principles.

clue.text: A single woman touring India, a foolish person

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit

indicators.note: touring says the woman's name goes round the letter for India

parts.note: Dot is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman travelling round India acts the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid or silly person.

clue.text: Lament matter suffering ill-use

indicators.note: suffering means damaged or in a bad way, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A complaint about mistreatment is being lodged.
explanation.definitionFit: Maltreatment is cruel or harsh treatment, which is what ill-use means as a noun.

clue.text: Extremely reliable, the first female magistrate in history

indicators.note: extremely means the outer letters of reliable

parts.note: the first and last letters of reliable
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: The first woman to serve as a magistrate was very dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official or chief magistrate in Anglo-Saxon and medieval England.

clue.text: Stop support for plant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... a flow is to stop it
second meaning: the stalk that holds a plant up

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an instruction to stop propping up a plant; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb meaning to halt and as a noun for a plant's main stalk.

clue.text: A composition finally being broadcast soon

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of composition

parts.note: the last letter of composition
on means on air, being broadcast

explanation.surface: A piece of music will shortly be on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for shortly or in a little while.

clue.text: Younger relative cut by retired writer

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the word for writer is read in reverse

parts.note: a pen is something to write with
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A young family member is cut out by a retired author.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephew is the son of one's sibling, a relative of a younger generation.

clue.text: Bony frame of English poet digesting opening of elegy

indicators.note: digesting means taking in, so the poet's name swallows the letter

parts.note: John Skelton was a Tudor English poet

indicators.note: opening of picks the first letter of elegy

parts.note: the first letter of elegy

explanation.surface: A thin English poet absorbs the start of a mournful verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is the framework of bones supporting a body.

clue.text: Small window in room secured by dynamic person

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the word for an active person

parts.note: a doer is an active, energetic person

explanation.surface: A little window in a room is fastened by an energetic worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormer is a window set upright in a sloping roof, often small.

clue.text: National flag at entrance to Holy Island

parts.note: a flag is an iris, the plant with sword-shaped leaves

indicators.note: entrance to picks the first letter of Holy

parts.note: the first letter of Holy
Man is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A national flag flies at the gateway to Holy Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is not a banner but the yellow flag iris; 'National' is a noun, a citizen of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irishman is a citizen of Ireland, a national of that country.
